extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, disciplinary counsel, and USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing imposition of reciprocal discipline by the USPTO (including eligibility for nunc pro tunc discipline, duties during suspension, waiver standards, and reinstatement procedures). Useful for practitioners subject to discipline and counsel handling USPTO disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: When another jurisdiction or Federal agency disciplines a USPTO practitioner, 'the USPTO Director ... shall impose ... identical reciprocal discipline except in limited circumstances.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director generally must impose identical discipline based on another jurisdiction's disciplinary action unless a limited, enumerated exception applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for nunc pro tunc reciprocal discipline (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may impose discipline nunc pro tunc only if the practitioner promptly notified the OED Director of his or her discipline in another jurisdiction, and establishes by clear and convincing evidence that the practitioner voluntarily ceased all activities related to practice before the Office and complied with all the duties of a suspended practitioner provided in § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners bear the burden of proof to show prompt notification and strict compliance with § 11.58. Compliance must be established 'entirely, not just substantially.' Failure to prove any required element (prompt notice, voluntary cessation, full compliance with § 11.58) renders the practitioner ineligible for nunc pro tunc reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt notification to OED (as prerequisite to nunc pro tunc)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Promptly notified the OED Director' of the discipline in another jurisdiction is a statutory prerequisite for backdating a USPTO suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner's failure to provide evidence of having notified the OED Director of the out-of-jurisdiction discipline undermines any request to have USPTO discipline imposed retroactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.58(b)(1)(i) — File notice of withdrawal from pending USPTO matters
rubrics_metrics.description: 'File a notice of withdrawal as of the effective date of the ... suspension ... in each pending patent and trademark application, each pending reexamination and interference or trial proceeding, and every other matter pending in the Office.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must file individual notices of withdrawal as required by § 11.58(b)(1)(i); shared customer numbers or partner associations do not excuse the practitioner's duty to withdraw. Admitted failure to withdraw defeats eligibility for nunc pro tunc discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.58(b)(1)(ii) — Provide notice to jurisdictions and certain clients
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Provide notice to all State and Federal jurisdictions and administrative agencies to which the practitioner is admitted to practice and all clients the practitioner represents having immediate prospective business before the Office ... of the order of [suspension] and of the practitioner's consequent inability to act as a practitioner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practitioner personally must provide the notices required by § 11.58(b)(1)(ii); constructive or indirect notice (e.g., another court's show-cause order) is insufficient. Lack of evidence that the practitioner provided these notices prevents nunc pro tunc relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.58(b)(1)(vi) — Remove advertising/representations of USPTO practice authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Take any necessary and appropriate steps to remove from any telephone, legal, or other directory any advertisement, statement, or representation which would reasonably suggest that the practitioner is authorized to practice patent, trademark, or other non-patent law before the Office.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must take reasonable steps (not merely honest mistakes) to ensure biographies, website listings, and other advertising do not misrepresent authorization to practice during suspension. Failure to demonstrate reasonable steps to remove such representations defeats eligibility for nunc pro tunc discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance standard: 'entirely, not just substantially' (interpretation of § 11.24 and § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must satisfy § 11.24 and § 11.58 'entirely, not just substantially' to be eligible for nunc pro tunc reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office requires strict compliance; partial or substantial compliance is inadequate. The standard of proof for showing compliance is 'clear and convincing evidence.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date for nunc pro tunc suspension (operative date of cessation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The effective date of a nunc pro tunc suspension 'shall be the date the practitioner voluntarily ceased all activities related to practice before the Office.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may backdate a suspension only to the date the practitioner actually ceased practice before the Office; failure to cease practice (e.g., by not withdrawing) means there is no earlier effective date to which the suspension may be backdated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of disciplinary regulation requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.3(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: 'In an extraordinary situation, when justice requires,' the USPTO Director or his delegee may waive any requirement of the disciplinary regulations which is not a requirement of statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver is strongly disfavored and will not be granted for circumstances that 'could have been prevented by the exercise of ordinary care or diligence.' The Office has limited examples of proper waiver (e.g., flood or fire preventing timely compliance). Mere misunderstanding of rules or good-faith mistakes are not extraordinary circumstances justifying waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: § 11.60 — Reinstatement prerequisites and public notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner may 'not resume practice' before the Office until reinstated by the OED Director and may 'apply for reinstatement only upon expiration of the period of [his or her] suspension, demonstrating 'full compliance with § 11.58,' and payment of a fee. Before reinstating, the OED Director shall publish a notice of the practitioner's petition for reinstatement and permit the public a reasonable opportunity to comment or submit evidence (§ 11.60(g)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinstatement requires demonstration of full compliance with § 11.58 and payment of the reinstatement fee; the public comment period is ordinarily required. The Office may, however, in extraordinary circumstances, waive the timing of publication (e.g., permit publication prior to expiration of suspension to align actual exclusion time with ordered suspension), and has waived § 11.60(g) in prior cases where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of suspension (Official Gazette and § 11.59 notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the Office's model notice of suspension and give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicizing the suspension and the reasons is part of the disciplinary process and is required by the regulations; the Official Gazette notice should include the basis for reciprocal discipline and links to OED FOIA documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office authority to dissociate practitioner from customer numbers and electronic accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate the practitioner's name from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s), if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissociation of customer numbers/accounts is an affirmative remedial step the Office may order to effectuate a practitioner's suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to satisfy § 11.58 precludes nunc pro tunc relief; waiver will not cure noncompliance absent extraordinary circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the Director were to waive some parts of § 11.58, failure to prove compliance with other required parts (e.g., § 11.58(b)(1)(ii)) means the practitioner remains ineligible for nunc pro tunc discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver requests that would not change the outcome are denied. Waiver is inappropriate where the practitioner's failure to comply could have been prevented by ordinary care or diligence; the burden remains on the practitioner to show extraordinary circumstances if seeking waiver.
